source_name: ČNB – REGIS (electronic submission portal and source of registration lists)
why_relevant: ČNB's electronic system for registration, licensing and notification submissions. It is the upstream feeder for several JERRS lists — vázaní zástupci (capital market, insurance distribution, supplementary pensions, consumer credit), samostatní zprostředkovatelé, akreditované osoby, pověření zástupci poskytovatelů platebních služeb, nebankovní poskytovatelé spotřebitelského úvěru. Understanding REGIS explains the latency and update cadence of the public lists; note it is a submission portal, not a public search interface.

Another well-established Czech register aggregator, notable for rendering ownership and officer relationship graphs and for surfacing extracted financial statement values per year. Helpful for fast triage of a payments vendor's size and connections before deciding whether to pull the underlying filings.

source_name: Chytrý rejstřík — commercial register with revenue and risk overlays
why_relevant: Aggregator positioning itself around 'tržby, rizika, vozidla, kontakty' and publishing explainers on exactly what the collection of deeds contains (financial statements, annual reports). Useful as a secondary index and, in particular, as a Czech-language reference for how filings are structured and labelled.

Newer Czech/Slovak media-monitoring platform frequently used by mid-sized brands; relevant as a lower-cost route to tracking pickup of banking and payments press releases across Czech online media. Recorded as unverified — the fetch failed at the TLS layer from this environment.

Named in the cell seed as a Czech financial news source. Confirmed live and published by Roklen Holding a.s., but the current site is materially narrower than the seed assumes: it is now an FX/currency-pair education and commentary property with an economic calendar, and does NOT carry bank ratings or traditional sell-side analyst research. Retained at low priority for its central-bank-decision calendar only.

Third-party aggregator that appears to compile the quarterly figures the building societies publish under Decree 163/2014 into cross-institution comparison tables. If it holds, it is a ready-made cross-check on our own parsing of the primary XLSX files and a fallback when an individual society's site is unreachable. Discovered as a search hit while chasing ČSOB Stavební spořitelna; not yet fetched, so treat scope and provenance as unconfirmed.

Named seed actor, verified live with a clean Czech structure (/reference/, /novinky/, /o-spolecnosti/, service pages for custom software, application maintenance, customer support and cybersecurity; 100+ staff, 30+ years). However its published references are public-sector and industrial — Ministry of Justice information systems since 1995, the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP — with no banking clients visible. Keep at low-frequency monitoring: it is a plausible bidder on state-owned bank work but is not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel.

Right-leaning news site and Týdeník Echo weekly; contributes commentary on bank windfall taxation, ČNB policy and state-vs-bank disputes. Included for completeness of the mainstream commentary spectrum; the guessed economy section path 404'd so its structure is unverified.

Czech news site tagged 'ekonomika, politika, byznys a finance', managed by Copywrite Company s.r.o., with sections spanning economics, politics, EU affairs, finance, business, investments, plus a podcasts/interviews section. Despite the fintech-suggestive name the observed coverage was general economic and political news (US debt, digital currencies, Czech pensions, pharma competition, Ukraine) rather than Czech retail-bank product or fee detail. Recorded here for completeness of the cell's media map and because its podcast/interview strand may carry Czech financial-sector executives, but yield for this cell's specific topics is unproven and looks thin.

Opinion-forward news site (publisher CMI News) with a standing EKONOMIKA desk and a large podcast slate; useful as a commentary/framing channel on banking taxation, windfall-tax debate and regulation. Verified on fetch that the section exists in navigation; note the masthead openly states a right-wing editorial perspective, so treat as commentary, not neutral reporting.

Long-running independent Czech register search site. Low unique value over the official register, but a useful fallback index and a source of alternate company-name spellings when the official search is strict about diacritics and legal-form suffixes.

High-volume English payments publication with an EMEA desk and cross-border payments coverage. Included for completeness of the English payments layer, but an on-site search for 'Czech' returned mostly EU-wide and Poland-centric items with no Czech-focused article on the first page - so Czech relevance is incidental rather than systematic.

source_name: ThePay, a.s. — corporate site (thepay.eu, formerly thepay.cz)
why_relevant: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, DIČ CZ28135261, Masarykovo náměstí 102/65, Jihlava) is one of the four domestic CZ gateway brands named in this cell. The old thepay.cz domain now 301-redirects to thepay.eu, itself a signal of a CEE-wide repositioning worth noting. Critically, on the pages inspected (homepage, /cs/kontakt/) there is NO blog, novinky or tiskové zprávy section — ThePay's public communications footprint is thin, so intelligence on it must come from statutory filings (Sbírka listin under IČO 28135261) and third-party press rather than from the company itself. Footer routes: /cs/napoveda/, /cs/kontakt/, /cs/pdf-verze/, /cs/partnersky-program-thepay/.

source_name: ČEFTAS Visualbook — association brand and identity assets
why_relevant: The Czech Fintech Association's brand portal, serving logos, typography and colour specifications in CZ/SK/EN. Marginal for market intelligence, but it confirms the ČEFTAS acronym and the association's Czech/Slovak dual-market positioning, and it is the kind of asset that dates rebrands — useful when reconciling historical references to the association under different names.
